rounds.text: Acme Resources Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by a market overly fixated on stale sentiment, ignoring powerful operational turnarounds where results score 81 out of 100 with net profit surging 100% year-on-year and earnings accelerating [E58]. The stock trades at an attractive price-to-book ratio of 0.51x against a book value of ₹ 52.4 [E2], sitting deeply discounted at just 14% of its 52-week range [E5]. Furthermore, the business is exceptionally well-capitalized with a debt-to-equity ratio of just 0.06x [E33], operating virtually debt-free [E45] alongside a comfortable short-term liquidity current ratio of 6.21x [E34]. Profits are also heavily backed by tangible strength, demonstrated by a phenomenal cash conversion of 7.11x that generated ₹ 10.09 Cr in both operating and free cash flow for March 2026 [E30, E31, E32]. Conceded: [E14, E20, E21, E25, E49] long-term sales growth has contracted and return on equity remains low at 1.72% over the last 3 years, yet the discounted cash flow intrinsic value of ₹ 28 still sits above the current market price of ₹ 26.6, providing an untapped margin of safety [E38, E49].

Acme Resources Ltd carries significant valuation and operational risks that are not supported by its depressed share price. The company exhibits severe top-line contraction across multiple horizons, including a 3-year compounded sales decline of -32% and a 10-year compounded sales decline of -12% [E16, E14]. This long-term revenue stagnation is compounded by deeply depressed profitability metrics, with a meager return on equity of 1.1% and return on capital employed of 1.7% [E13, E12], both lagging far behind broader sector benchmarks [E9, E10]. Valuation multiples also present a distinct disconnect: the stock trades at an elevated P/E of 59x against a sector benchmark of 18.53x and an EV/EBITDA of 35.69x compared to its sector benchmark of 12.91x [E6, E11]. Furthermore, despite reporting repeated profits, the company offers a dividend yield of 0.00% [E4, E47] and its reported earnings are dependent on non-operating sources, including Rs 1.73 Cr of other income [E50]. Conceded: the company demonstrates low leverage, a comfortable current ratio of 6.21x, and robust recent cash conversion backed by Rs 10.09 Cr of operating and free cash flow [E33, E34, E30, E31, E32]. Nevertheless, the persistent erosion of its core business scale and inflated valuation multiples relative to sector norms expose investors to substantial downside risk [E16, E6, E11].

The bear’s focus on long-term sales contraction ignores the critical reality that the company is currently in a state of accelerating turnaround, with recent profit growth significantly outpacing price performance [E42, E55]. While the bear highlights historical revenue declines [E14, E16], it overlooks the fact that the company is now generating robust, high-quality cash flows, with operating and free cash flow reaching Rs 10.09 Cr in Mar 2026 [E31, E32]. Conceded: the company has delivered poor sales growth over the past five years [E48] and currently offers no dividend [E4, E47]. However, the bear’s critique of valuation multiples is misleading; while the P/E is high, the stock trades at a significant discount to book value at 0.51x, which is substantially lower than the sector benchmark of 1.29x [E2, E7, E46]. Furthermore, the company’s financial health is exceptionally strong, characterized by a conservative debt-to-equity ratio of 0.06x and a liquidity-rich current ratio of 6.21x, providing a massive safety buffer that the bear fails to weigh against its operational concerns [E33, E34, E45]. Finally, the bear’s reliance on stale long-term averages ignores the most recent evidence of a 100% year-over-year net profit increase, which suggests the business is successfully pivoting toward a more profitable trajectory [E52, E58].

The bull claims an accelerating turnaround [E55] and points to high operating cash flow [E31], but ignores that earnings are artificially inflated by Rs 1.73 Cr of other income [E50]. Conceded: the company trades at a price-to-book of 0.51x against a sector benchmark of 1.29x [E7, E46], yet this asset discount merely reflects chronically depressed capital efficiency, specifically a median 10-year return on equity of 1% and a current ROE of just 1.1% [E13, E26]. While the bull celebrates debt levels [E33, E45], it glosses over the structural top-line decay shown by a 10-year compounded sales contraction of -12% and a 3-year drop of -32% [E14, E16]. Furthermore, the bull's reliance on recent profit growth [E52] ignores the reality that compounded profit growth over 3 years is -51% and over the trailing twelve months is -22% [E20, E21]. Finally, despite reporting profits, the company continues to withhold a payout entirely, leaving the dividend yield at 0.00% [E4, E47].
